goal: Survey figures (SU1): app/survey.py with questions, Likert scales, question bars with Other, Likert and cross-tab kinds, Respondents histograms, export list (Board gate 183 scales agree/satisfied/likely/frequency/1-5/1-7 and Respondents; gate 184 amount guard and full scale with zero counts)

acceptance_criteria.text: survey.questions(columns, mapping, typed) returns the categorical columns plus the whole-number 1..5/1..7 answer columns in column order; time, identifier and other numerical columns are not questions

survey.scale(values) returns (levels, neutral index) or None: ['Agree','neutral'] is the agree scale, [1,3,7] the 1..7 scale, ['Never','Often'] the frequency scale, ['yes','no'] gives None; all levels are kept even with a count of 0, in the data's own spelling when present

A non-Likert question gives a kind 'bar' dict with orientation 'h', counts per value sorted count desc then name, top 10 then one 'Other' (other: true); on survey_rows() city gives city00..city03 4, city04..city09 3, Other 6; gender female 14, male 13, other 13
A Likert question gives kind 'likert' with data levels, counts, pct (unrounded, sums to 100) and neutral index; q_service counts 6,6,6,16,6 and pct 15,15,15,40,15; q_visits 9,9,9,9,4

survey.pick(questions, row, col) returns the two names from the URL when both are questions, else the first two; the cross-tab dict kind 'crosstab' has x column levels, y row levels, z counts and row pct (each row sums to 100); gender x region gives female 3,4,3,4 (21.4, 28.6, 21.4, 28.6%), male 3,3,4,3, other 4,3,3,3; levels in scale order for Likert questions else count desc then name
Respondents: up to 2 numerical columns that are not answers and not plain (identifier/year-like), as histograms; survey.csv has age only (respondent_id is an identifier)

survey.export(view) returns one bar per question (Likert as a bar of counts in scale order), then the cross-tab as a table chart, then the Respondents histograms; payload has charts in order questions, cross-tab, Respondents with ids chart-1..N plus questions and pick; tests/test_survey.py checks the hand values recomputed from survey_rows()
Moves acceptance items AC-68, AC-69, AC-70, AC-71 forward
